- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.6) — reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to sentiment strength.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (e.g., >80) — add 1–3% buffer to prevent undershoot.
- Lagged corrections: if sentiment turns positive after a dip, forecast should rise 1–2 days before true price rebound.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overreact to short-term sentiment — dampen momentum by 10–15% if sentiment is volatile or low.
- Overshoot after spikes: if forecast exceeds true outcome by >3% after a spike, reduce by 1–2% per day until price stabilizes.
- Sentiment-driven bias: if sentiment > 0.7, forecast should be 1–2% below true outcome to avoid overconfidence in upward momentum.
